Boat trailer repair: bearings, hubs, brakes, lights, winches, bunks

A boat trailer dunked in salt water every weekend needs more than most owners give it. Bearings, hubs, surge brakes, lights, and bunks, done in your driveway so you make the ramp on Saturday.

When
Annually, or at any hub heat, grinding, pulling under braking, or lights out.
Time on site
1 to 3 hours
What it usually costs here
$150 to $400 for bearings and lights; brake jobs $300 to $800; bunk and roller work quoted.

What's included

  • Bearing repack or hub replacement, Bearing Buddies
  • Surge or electric brake service, actuators, lines
  • LED light conversion and wiring harness
  • Winch, strap, bow stop, and safety chains
  • Bunk boards and carpet, rollers
  • Tires, spare, and jack
  • Coupler and tongue inspection

In Tampa Bay specifically

Ramp-launch boats are the norm in Pasco and south Hillsborough: Hudson Beach, Nick's Park, E.G. Simmons, Williams Park. Trailer failures on US-19 and I-75 are a weekly sight in season.

Questions we get

How often should bearings be repacked in salt water?

Once a year for a weekend boat. Flush the hubs after every launch and check for heat at the first stop.

Can you come to the storage lot?

Yes, with the lot's permission.
